I think this is correct. In some ways it is similar to the socialism vs. competitive market (Adam Smith Capitalism) argument. Socialists believe there is only one pie, so we must cut it up evenly. Adam Smith Capitalist believe we can just bake more pie. To complete the analogy, those against AI think there are only so many possible jobs, and we must protect those jobs. Better thinkers know that the need to do our current jobs the way we do them is exactly what's holding us back from so many other "better" things we could be doing with our time. Farming is a good example. Back in the 1920's, 30% of the US population worked in agriculture (32 million people). Now, only 1.9 million people (les than 2%) work in agriculture. Yet it seems like we are much richer, have more food, and everyone has an XBox and a smart phone now, and not then. (I used AI to get those stats, so even my commenting is more efficient with AI.) What we did was redeploy those people to new tasks that raised the overall level of wealth in society. Sure, the rich got fabulously wealthy, but the rising tide really did lift all boats. If instead we'd have banned tractors and "protected the family farm", we probably never could have gone to the moon or ended up with internet beaming down to every corner of the earth from friendly satellites. Never underestimate people's ability to want more. But for everyone to have more, we need to produce more for less. Socialism won't do it, it's fair in that everyone ends up with less. But increasing productivity, even when not distributed perfectly fairly, means a much larger pie to divvy up. And history has shown time and time again that you can tweak Adam Smith Capitalism to be more fair, but you cannot tweak socialism to be more productive.
